answer: Persistent Reef Anchoring prevents sybil attacks by requiring new identities to demonstrate consistent cross-epoch activity before gaining full economic rights. Each identity must establish a behavioral reef by logging verifiable actions across epochs, with early penalties applied if activity drops below threshold. Attackers face a hollow trap where creating multiple identities doubles their cost, as each false anchor must still be maintained across time. The mechanism operates like a wharf system, where only those who dock consistently across epochs earn passage to full privileges.
